clue.text: Chancy fierce run? MCC, note, gets a boundary

indicators.note: something chancy is random and unpredictable, so the letters that follow are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the Marylebone Cricket Club
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A risky run at cricket brings a boundary, with the game's governing club taking note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chancy' shuffles FIERCE, RUN, MCC and E together. The cricket picture of runs and boundaries hides a geometric boundary: the line round a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The perimeter of a circle is its bounding line, so it is a boundary in the geometric sense.

clue.text: Angry allusion to another passage?

parts.note: read playfully, an annoyed mention would be a cross one; really it is a note in a book directing the reader elsewhere in the text

explanation.surface: Someone makes a bad-tempered remark about a different section of a text.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer in a book that sends the reader to a related entry or page elsewhere is exactly this kind of note.

clue.text: Sincere maiden's in a state

parts.note: sincere means real, genuine
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An earnest young woman finds herself in a nervous state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' looks like an idiom for being flustered; 'state' alone is the definition, a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom or domain ruled as one country counts as a state.

clue.text: Lacking appreciation for a French quantity of coal

parts.note: un is French for a
read whimsically, enough coal to fill a fireplace grate is a grate-ful

explanation.surface: Someone is unimpressed by being offered just a French measure of coal.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the invented measure 'grate-ful', like 'spoonful', the amount a fire grate holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fails to show thanks for a kindness is lacking appreciation.

clue.text: University doctor was first to go under Flamborough Head but made a hash of it

indicators.note: in a down answer, pieces that go under another come after it in the grid
the head of a word is its first letter, here the start of Flamborough

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
to lead is to be first, so led means was first

explanation.surface: A university medic took the lead beneath Flamborough Head, a Yorkshire headland, but bungled it.
explanation.walkthrough: Flamborough Head is a real Yorkshire headland, which disguises 'Head' as the first-letter signal. In a down clue 'to go under' puts UMBLED below F.
explanation.definitionFit: To fumble something is to handle it clumsily, botching the job.

clue.text: Caused irritation in a joint, in a way

indicators.note: the second in says one piece sits inside the other, the joint within the way

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: Something gave pain in a joint, in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' sounds like a hedge meaning 'somewhat', but 'way' is a road, RD, around ANKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankled festered and annoyed, leaving lasting resentment.

clue.text: Nothing oriental about this flower

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: This bloom has nothing eastern about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' in crosswords is often a river, something that flows; here the Egyptian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, so crosswords call it a flower.

clue.text: Detailed the Spanish seaman to make a speech

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
to orate is to deliver a speech

explanation.surface: A Spanish sailor was told off to address the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as a verb, assigned to a task; it is the adjective meaning intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worked out with much intricacy and many parts is detailed.

clue.text: Vegetable — cockney's present, say, to boxer (if he hits him right)

definitions.text: to boxer (if he hits him right)

parts.note: a cauliflower is a vegetable

indicators.note: say tells us that the cockney word is spoken, matching a word that sounds the same

parts.note: present means here, and a cockney drops the h to say 'ere

explanation.surface: A vegetable is handed over in a cockney accent to a boxer who lands a good punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift; it is 'here', which a cockney (a working-class Londoner who drops the h) says as 'ere'. The definition is what a boxer gives an opponent he hits well.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated blows swell and deform a boxer's outer organ of hearing into a lumpy shape, a classic fighting injury.

clue.text: Member of political society takes fruit to the island

parts.note: an orange is a fruit
the Isle of Man, often just Man in crosswords

explanation.surface: A party activist carries fruit over to the island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant society in Northern Ireland; its members bear this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Orange Order, the Ulster Protestant society, is known by this title.

clue.text: A claw-back from an overseas plant

indicators.note: back says the word for claw is read from right to left

parts.note: a claw is a nail, as on an animal's toe

explanation.surface: A clawback of money from a foreign plant, a factory abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claw-back' reads as a refund; split, 'back' turns NAIL into LIAN, followed by the A at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A woody climbing vine of tropical forests is a plant found abroad.

clue.text: It leads doctor to a group of islands

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: Something guides a doctor to an archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is crossword slang for sex appeal, SA, which leads MO and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific nation is made up of several islands, an archipelago.

clue.text: This girl's something special

explanation.surface: This young woman is a remarkable one.
explanation.walkthrough: One reading is a girl's name; the other is slang for a remarkable thing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, as of the singer, and also slang for an outstanding person or thing.

clue.text: It's work to the Italian

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Labour is bound for the Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labour or exertion is work.

clue.text: No star more involved such a man

definitions.text: No star more involved such a man

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: No man is more caught up with the stars than this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles NO, STAR and MORE; the whole clue also describes a stargazer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies stars is deeply involved with them.

clue.text: Encourage the chief to be intellectual

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage
a chief is a head, a leader

explanation.surface: Urge the boss to be clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookish, highly cerebral person is called an intellectual.

clue.text: Country fete includes aristocratic team perhaps

indicators.note: includes says the word for fete holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a gala is a fete, a festive event
U means upper-class

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word team may be put into another order

explanation.surface: A national fete features a team of nobles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TEAM into ATEM; U plus ATEM go inside GALA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central American nation is a country.

clue.text: The lady has the workers in a cleft stick

parts.note: Di is a lady's name, short for Diana
staff are the workers of a firm

explanation.surface: A woman has her employees in a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a cleft stick' is an idiom for being in a fix, but here a cleft stick is the definition: the stick holding wool for spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked rod that holds unspun wool or flax is a cleft stick used in spinning.

clue.text: The age undoubtedly is being, scratched out

parts.note: an era is an age
sure means certain, undoubtedly

explanation.surface: This era is certainly one being wiped away.
explanation.definitionFit: Deletion is the act of rubbing out, so something being scratched out undergoes it.

clue.text: Cheer up English film star invest money in him!

indicators.note: in, after invest, places the money inside the film star's name

parts.note: David Niven was a British film star
L is the pound sign, money

explanation.surface: Cheer up an English movie star by putting money into him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' leads the reader to finance, but it is part of the putting-inside instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To liven or brighten someone's spirits is to cheer them up.

clue.text: Depot or material for a missile

indicators.note: material as in raw material, words to be reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A depot or materials store for missiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' sounds like stock in a depot; it signals that DEPOT and OR are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwater self-propelled weapon is a missile.

clue.text: They shed light on a revolutionary in the hills

indicators.note: in says the revolutionary is placed within the hills

parts.note: tors are rocky hills
Che Guevara was a revolutionary

explanation.surface: They illuminate a rebel hiding out in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaming brands or electric lamps carried in hand illuminate the dark.

clue.text: They see and hear agreements

indicators.note: hear says the word for agreements is to be taken as heard, matching a word with the same sound

parts.note: ayes are yes votes, agreements

explanation.surface: Delegates watch and listen to motions being carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Organs of sight are what see.

clue.text: To drink endlessly is a disgrace

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for drink is cut off

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily

explanation.surface: Drinking without stopping is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' looks like 'without stopping', but it cuts the end from SLURP.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is a stain on someone's reputation, a disgrace.

clue.text: Chemical interchange

indicators.note: change says the letters of inter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemical swap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interchange' is one word; split, 'inter' is rearranged by 'change'.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate, saltpetre, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: The precept can go up as well as down

indicators.text: can go up as well as down
indicators.note: in a down answer, a word that reads the same going up as going down is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A principle that can rise as well as fall, like an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the warning that investments can go down as well as up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine held as true, a precept.

clue.text: Invented cheese?

parts.note: invented means made, and the word for made read backwards is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: Someone has dreamt up a new cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A round Dutch cheese with a red wax coat whose letters run backwards to a word for invented.

clue.text: This vegetable's burnt, I say

indicators.note: I say marks the word as spoken, so it is matched by its sound

parts.note: charred means burnt

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that their vegetable is burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like an exclamation; it signals that CHARRED sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy green beet grown for its stalks and leaves is a vegetable.

clue.text: After wartime victory strong men went to church showing fervour

parts.note: VE Day marked Victory in Europe in 1945
he-men are strong, macho men
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: After the war was won, tough men went to church with passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Great intensity of feeling is fervour.

clue.text: The manager wants to order a rota — mind it's right!

indicators.note: to order means to arrange in sequence, so these letters are sorted into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, the letters I, T, S

explanation.surface: The boss needs to arrange a rota, and insists it is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' scrambles A, ROTA, MIND and IT'S, then R for right finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who runs an organisation's affairs is its manager.
